clue.text: A month almost on cold spicy food like this?

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: almost means the month's name stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: June is a month of the year

explanation.surface: A recipe query: spice up a dish in a month's time, served cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' clips the month by a letter; 'on' in an across clue means following, so the cold letter leads despite coming last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cajun cooking, from Louisiana, is famous for its heavily spiced dishes such as jambalaya and gumbo.

clue.text: Plant pot under settee

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts this piece below the other

parts.note: a couch is a settee or sofa
grass and pot are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A potted plant tucked beneath the sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' looks like a plant pot but is the drug, GRASS, written 'under' COUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Couch grass is a creeping weed, a common plant of gardens and fields.

clue.text: Short film talk

indicators.note: short means the film title loses its last letter

parts.note: Jaws is Spielberg's 1975 shark film

explanation.surface: A brief chat about movies.
explanation.definitionFit: To jaw is informal for to talk at length, chatter.

clue.text: Hold in Lady Hamilton's arms?

definitions.meaning: a wrestling grip, such as the full or half version
Admiral Lord ... was the famous lover of Emma, Lady Hamilton

explanation.surface: Is the person held in Lady Hamilton's embrace a wrestler?
explanation.definitionFit: A nelson is a wrestling hold, and Horatio Nelson was Lady Hamilton's lover.

clue.text: Painter in blue?

definitions.meaning: John ..., the English landscape painter of The Hay Wain
a police officer of the lowest rank, dressed in a blue uniform

explanation.definitionFit: Constable is both a famous English painter's surname and the rank of an ordinary police officer in blue.

clue.text: U-turn makes Conservative member sad

parts.note: a limb, an arm or leg, is a member of the body
feeling down is feeling sad

explanation.surface: A political reversal leaves a Tory MP unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' suggests a member of Parliament but is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb-down is a retreat from a firm position, a reversal or U-turn.

clue.text: This river's African Queen nearly capsized

definitions.note: a statement: the river named is in Africa

indicators.note: capsized means the shortened word is turned upside down, read upwards
nearly means the last letter of the Latin queen is dropped

parts.note: Regina is Latin for queen

explanation.surface: The boat from the film The African Queen almost overturned on this river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims REGINA to REGIN and 'capsized' turns it over in the down clue. The African Queen, in italics, is the novel and Bogart film.
explanation.definitionFit: The Niger is a great river of West Africa, flowing through Mali and Nigeria.

clue.text: Film live, standing during intervals

indicators.note: during means one piece goes in the middle of the other

parts.note: thirds are musical intervals

indicators.note: standing in a down clue means the word is set upright, read from the bottom

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A film made live, with people standing in the breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' in a down clue sets the verb upright (EB); 'during' drops it into musical intervals, the sense 'intervals' hides behind its everyday meaning of breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Birds is Alfred Hitchcock's 1963 thriller film.

clue.text: Capital letters, the last repeated, are visible at first among letters not designed to be seen

indicators.note: among means the gathered letters sit within the word for tactile writing

parts.words: letters not designed to be seen
parts.note: Braille is raised writing read by touch, not sight

indicators.note: repeated means the final letter of the alphabet appears twice

parts.note: the last of the letters of the alphabet is Z
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of visible is used

explanation.surface: A capital, spelt with doubled final letters, visible at first among unseen letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters, the last' means the alphabet's final letter, doubled by 'repeated'; 'among' places the group inside the tactile script, after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazzaville is the capital city of the Republic of the Congo.

clue.text: Painter inspired by quiet types

indicators.note: inspired by means breathed in by the words, so the answer lies within them

explanation.surface: An artist drawing inspiration from the silent sort.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'quiET TYpes'.
explanation.definitionFit: William Etty was an English painter famous for his nudes, a crossword favourite.

clue.text: Those leaving nothing, legally so resistant?

definitions.meaning: people who die leaving no will are, read playfully, without a will: intestate
reluctant, not willing to do something

explanation.surface: A lawyer muses on people who leave nothing and resist the law.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the answer as UN + WILL + ING: having no will, so leaving nothing legally.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reluctant or resistant to doing something is being not willing, the ordinary meaning of the word.

clue.text: Spot on patient's bottom beginning to congeal, cut from behind

indicators.note: from behind means the word for cut is read backwards

parts.note: to axe something is to cut it

indicators.note: beginning to points at the first letter of the following word, congeal
the bottom of a word in an across clue is its last letter, here of patient's

explanation.surface: A medical note about a spot on a patient's backside starting to congeal and being cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from behind' gives EXA; 'beginning to' and 'bottom' each pick one letter. 'Spot' tempts as a blemish on the patient, but 'Spot on' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exact is precisely right, which is what spot on means colloquially.

clue.text: French romantic has hassle with British queen, Elizabeth stealing ring

parts.note: to hector is to bully or hassle someone
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of the Queen

indicators.note: stealing means the shortened name takes something into itself

parts.note: Liz is a short form of the name Elizabeth
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A French romantic hero bothers a British queen while Elizabeth pinches a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stealing' has LIZ take in O, giving LIOZ. ER for queen is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector Berlioz was the leading French composer of the Romantic movement, author of the Symphonie fantastique.

clue.text: Letter saying something cutting

parts.note: a circular is a letter sent to many people
a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: A letter with a stinging remark in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something cutting' sounds like a barbed remark but is a literal cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular saw is a power tool with a toothed disc for cutting wood.

clue.text: He observed wood bound by rope lifted over head

indicators.note: over in a down clue means this piece sits above the next
bound by means the wood is held inside the reversed word
lifted in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: to tie is to rope or bind
yew is a wood
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A man watched wood being roped and hauled over somebody's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns the binding verb upward, EIT; 'bound by' wraps it round the tree; 'over' stacks the result on a headland, a sense of 'head' common in place names.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyewitness is a person who saw an event happen, so he observed it.

clue.text: Might a four-leaf clover be so red?

definitions.text: Might a four-leaf clover be so
definitions.meaning: four-leaf clovers are uncommon, hard to find
meat cooked very lightly, still red inside

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about whether lucky clover could be red.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare means uncommon, as a four-leaf clover is, and also describes underdone, red meat.

clue.text: No scoring with bird through the years, becoming sentimental

parts.note: love is a score of nothing in tennis

indicators.note: through means the bird runs through the middle of the two letters

parts.note: Y is an abbreviation for year, so two of them stand for years
a dove is a bird

explanation.surface: A goalless lover with a girlfriend over the years turns soppy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' puts DOVE between the two Ys, giving YDOVEY. Love for nil comes from tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovey-dovey describes cloyingly affectionate, sentimental behaviour between lovers.

clue.text: Catching sozzled grannies sinking last of gin

indicators.note: sinking means the grannies swallow a letter as if drinking it
sozzled means drunk, so the letters reel into a new order
last of takes the final letter of gin

explanation.surface: Tipsy grandmothers knocking back the last of the gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sozzled' scrambles GRANNIES; 'sinking' has them take in N, the final letter picked by 'last of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensnaring is trapping or catching, as in a snare.

clue.text: Conversation with little girl unending sweet

parts.note: craic or crack is Irish for lively chat

indicators.note: unending means the girl's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Little Nell is the child heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop

explanation.surface: Chatting with a small girl about an endless supply of sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Nell is from Dickens; 'unending' trims NELL to NEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracknel is a crisp brittle confection or biscuit, often made with nuts.

clue.text: Queen's failed to welcome a republican aboard ship, showing honesty

indicators.note: aboard means everything else is placed inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: to welcome means the scrambled letters take the next pieces inside them
failed signals that the queen's letters collapse into a new order

parts.note: the word Queen with its 's read as an extra S letter
R is the abbreviation for Republican, as in US politics

explanation.surface: A monarch fails to greet a republican on board ship, which says something about integrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed' gives QUENES; 'to welcome' takes in A and R, making QUARENES; 'aboard' puts it inside the steamship letters, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Squareness is honesty or fairness, as in dealing square or a square deal.

clue.text: Stream where Lothario's laid back

indicators.note: laid back means the word for a womaniser lies backwards

parts.note: a Lothario, or seducer, is a wolf

explanation.surface: The stream is where a seducer lounges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid back' looks like 'relaxed' but turns WOLF round. Lothario is the seducer in an old play, hence any womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: A flow is a moving stream of liquid, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Millions I kill, only to lose

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for million
to slay is to kill

explanation.surface: A mass killer boasts of millions of victims, only to lose.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislay something is to lose it by forgetting where it was put.

clue.text: Backing old man, keeping quiet, I'm feeding stress

indicators.note: feeding means the other pieces go into the word for stress

parts.note: accent is stress on a syllable

indicators.note: keeping means the man holds the next letter inside

parts.note: taken as written
P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
I'm without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Supporting an elderly fellow while keeping silent and feeding his stress.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text added a stray 'A'. 'keeping' gives MPAN; 'feeding' puts the old man run inside the stress word after its third letter. 'Backing' looks like support for a person but is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: An accompaniment is a musical backing, the part supporting a soloist or singer.

clue.text: Wrongly placed, I am a South African

indicators.note: wrongly placed means the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone misplaced claims to be South African.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South African' looks like one nationality, but South supplies S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masai are a people of Kenya and Tanzania, so a Masai is an East African.

clue.text: Sweet defined as otherwise?

definitions.meaning: a pastry dessert with a filling
sour or sharp, the opposite of sweet

explanation.surface: A dessert described as its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart is a sweet pastry, yet tart also means sharp-tasting, the reverse of sweet.

clue.text: Property going up for which one may go down?

definitions.text: Property going up for which one may go down?

parts.words: Property going up for which one may go down?
parts.note: property going up in flames, a crime for which an offender may go down, that is to prison

explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the crime of setting fire to property, which can lead to a prison sentence.

clue.text: Picture nevertheless requiring long sentence

parts.note: still means nevertheless, as in 'still, it worked'
a life sentence is the longest prison term

explanation.surface: An artwork that nevertheless demands a lengthy prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: A still life is a painting or picture of inanimate objects such as fruit or flowers.

clue.text: Every so often, dislike being kind

indicators.note: every so often means taking letters at regular intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: Disliking someone only occasionally is a sort of kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: The 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of dIsLiKe are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilk means kind or sort, as in 'people of that ilk'.

clue.text: Measure of material in drawing cloth

indicators.note: in means the measure sits inside the word for drawing

parts.note: towing is drawing or pulling along
the ell was an old measure of cloth, about 45 inches

explanation.surface: Some cloth measured out for an artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' suggests art but means pulling; 'in' places the old cloth measure inside it, which also echoes the 'material' of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Towelling is the absorbent looped cotton fabric used to make towels.

clue.text: Sure to stash one grand that was hot!

indicators.note: to stash means the agreement word hides the next letters inside

parts.note: sure! and yes! both express agreement
I is the Roman numeral one
K, for kilo, means a thousand, a grand

explanation.surface: A thief agrees to hide a thousand pounds of stolen, hot money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stash' puts I and K inside YES. 'hot' in the surface means stolen; in the definition it means scorching.
explanation.definitionFit: Yikes is an exclamation of alarm, the kind of cry uttered on touching something scalding.
